requirements.requirement: Establish a usable integrity baseline covering /etc on node1.
requirements.summary: A root-protected SHA-256 manifest was initialized with 1,318 entries, and the final check directly showed that /etc matched the baseline. Four boot/runtime-derived files were deliberately excluded; this is a reasonable noise-control choice rather than evidence that general /etc coverage is absent.

requirements.requirement: Allow later changes under /etc to be identified and reported.
requirements.summary: Controlled additions under /etc produced path, metadata, and SHA-256 details with alert status 1. A reboot also directly produced CHANGED reports for modified files. Reports were persisted, both probes were removed, and the final integrity check was clean. A protected daily cron hook provides ongoing execution.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation successfully used the installed legacy coreutils and shell facilities. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged in final observations.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 has a protected /etc integrity baseline, controlled changes are detected and logged, daily checking is configured, and the legacy OS and kernel were preserved. The provider restart protocol demonstrated a real reboot and recovery, but it was not repeated after the final checker edit and baseline reinitialization.
limitations: The mandatory restart occurred before cmd-1ff240fa89a34c8d modified the checker and reinitialized the final baseline. Thus the fixed boot identities and reboot evidence prove a genuine restart, but not persistence of the exact final implementation through a subsequent restart.

The four excluded runtime-derived files are not themselves monitored; evidence does not independently inspect every claimed authoritative source, although general /etc coverage and change detection are directly demonstrated.
The lifecycle package-health probe is unsupported in practice on this legacy yum version because it printed yum usage in both snapshots, so package consistency cannot be independently assessed.
Final lifecycle collection inventories /tmp but not /var/tmp, leaving the disposition of the reboot log created by cmd-f4db52f8d8c0495c uncertain.

operational_hygiene.summary: The task mutations were generally necessary and controlled: installation and baseline creation supported the required outcome, integrity probes were bounded and removed, and the post-restart baseline refinement corrected observed runtime noise. One unnecessary low-risk mutation was identified: cmd-f4db52f8d8c0495c redirected reboot output to /var/tmp/etc-integrity-reboot.log, but that file was never used as evidence or explicitly cleaned. Whether it remained is indeterminate because the final temporary-file inventory did not cover /var/tmp. No new listening sockets, /tmp residue, platform change, or demonstrated package damage appeared in lifecycle observations.
